summary: George de Roerich worked in Tibetology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the universities of London, Harvard, and Paris under scholars including Minorsky, Lévi, and Lanman, later serving as director of the Urusvati Himalayan Research Institute.

George van Driem is a linguist and Tibetologist who studied at the University of Virginia and Leiden University. He held positions at Leiden University, including chair of Descriptive Linguistics (1999–2009), and was Professor of Historical Linguistics at Bern (2010–2022).

Georges B. J. Dreyfus specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics and under Jeffrey Hopkins at the University of Virginia, later becoming Jackson Professor of Religion at Williams College.

Georges Dumézil was a scholar of linguistics, religious studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied under Antoine Meillet. His career included posts at Istanbul University, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the Collège de France (1949–1968).

Georges Perrot was an archaeologist and historian who studied at the École Normale Supérieure in 1852. He later held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, the University of Paris, and served as director of the École Normale Supérieure.

Georges-Jean Pinault is a linguist specializing in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure, Sorbonne Nouvelle, and EPHE, and held professorial posts at Blaise Pascal University and the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Georgios T. Halkias is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his DPhil under Charles Ramble at the University of Oxford and later became an associate professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Hong Kong around 2012.

Gerald Hüther studied at the University of Leipzig from 1969 to 1974. He worked at the Max Planck Institute for Experimental Medicine from 1979 to 1989 and later held posts at the University of Göttingen and Universitätsmedizin Göttingen.

Gerald James Larson specialized in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, earning degrees from Union Theological Seminary and Columbia University. He was a professor of Religious Studies at UC Santa Barbara and Rabindranath Tagore Professor Emeritus at Indiana University.
Gerardus van der Leeuw was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Leiden University from roughly 1908 to 1916 and held a post at the University of Groningen from 1918 to 1950.

Gereon Kopf specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. After studying at Temple University, he conducted research at J. F. Oberlin University and the Nanzan Institute, later serving as Associate Professor for Asian and Comparative Religions at Luther College.

Gergely Hidas works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University and completed his DPhil under Alexis Sanderson at the University of Oxford, later holding posts at Eötvös Loránd University and the British Museum.

Gerhard Oberhammer was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Innsbruck and under Erich Frauwallner. After a post at Utrecht University, he served as professor at the University of Vienna from 1964 to 1997.

Gerhard Wolf is a historian and archaeologist who studied at the University of Heidelberg from 1973 to 1989. He held posts at the University of Berlin and Trier University, and joined the Max Planck Society around 2003.
Gernot Böhme was a philosopher who studied at the University of Hamburg from around 1961 to 1965. He subsequently held a post at the Technical University of Darmstadt from roughly 1977 to 2002.

Gerrit Jan Meulenbeld was an Indologist who studied at Utrecht University from around 1946 to 1974 under Jan Gonda. In 1978, he served as an associate professor of Indology at the University of Groningen.

Gert Klingenschmitt specialized in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed his PhD under Karl Hoffmann at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg, taught there, and later held the chair of Indogermanistik at the University of Regensburg (1983–2006).

Geshe Gendun Lodro was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who completed his geshe studies at Drepung Gomang Dratsang. He held academic posts at the University of Hamburg starting in 1967 and visited the University of Virginia in 1979.

Geshe Jampa Tegchok specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology and studied at Sera Monastery. He served as abbot and resident teacher at Nalanda Monastery (~1982–1993) and later as resident teacher at the Land of Medicine Buddha (~1998–2001).
Geshe Karma Sonam is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Gyume Tantric Monastery, attested in 1987, and at Sera Monastery, attested in 1992.
